name: Fruit Bread Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ¼ lb. raisins, seeded and chopped
ingredients.originalText: ¼ lb. raisins, seeded and chopped

ingredients.name: ¼ lb. currants, well washed and picked over
ingredients.originalText: ¼ lb. currants, well washed and picked over

ingredients.name: soda, dissolved in hot water
ingredients.originalText: 1 teaspoonful soda, dissolved in hot water

ingredients.name: scant cups fine bread-crumbs, from a stale loaf
ingredients.originalText: 2 scant cups fine bread-crumbs, from a stale loaf

instructions.text: Beat the yolks light with the sugar
Add the bread-crumbs when they have been well soaked in the milk, and stir until smooth
Put in the fruit, well dredged with flour, the soda, and finally the whites, whipped to a stiff froth
Cover it if it threatens to harden too soon on top
Send to table hot in the dish in which it was baked, or turn out very carefully upon a hot plate

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Beat the yolks light with the sugar
2. Add the bread-crumbs when they have been well soaked in the milk, and stir until smooth
3. Put in the fruit, well dredged with flour, the soda, and finally the whites, whipped to a stiff froth
4. Cover it if it threatens to harden too soon on top
5. Send to table hot in the dish in which it was baked, or turn out very carefully upon a hot plate
6. Eat warm, with pudding-sauce
